deferred_follow_up: Single-process per-agent token-bucket enforcement has real mutation evidence, but complete agent-velocity abuse resistance remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP. The conformance test admits the first request, denies a repeated request for the same identity under a one-request ceiling, and admits a different agent through an independent bucket. It does not coordinate counters across processes, exercise the per-session ceiling, resist attackers that rotate agent identities, or prove secure limits are enabled in production. Follow-up work must qualify distributed counters, combined agent and session limits, identity-cost or Sybil controls, and deployment configuration.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/agent_velocity_abuse.rs configures AgentVelocityGuard with a one-request per-agent ceiling. It requires the first request to allow, the second request from the same agent to deny, and a request from another agent to allow. A targeted cargo-mutants run replaced the agent_velocity.rs TokenBucket::can_consume method with true; the repeated same-agent assertion caught the exhaustion bypass while the identity-isolation controls remained meaningful. PARTIAL: distributed state, session ceilings, multi-identity amplification, and production limit configuration remain deferred.
